test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 28 Nov, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: Liberalisation means:

options.text: increase in restrictions on imports and exports
increase in control of government over the private sector
reduction in control of government over the private sector
free play of market forces in all sectors with no controls

solution:
The correct answer is __**reduction in control of government over the private sector**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Liberalisation** refers to the process of reducing government restrictions and regulations in an economy to enhance the ease of doing business and promote economic activities.
 
• This typically involves **reducing tariffs, trade barriers, and government monopolies**, and allowing greater competition and private sector participation.
 
• The primary aim is to **increase economic efficiency and stimulate growth** by allowing market forces to determine prices and production.
 
• Countries often implement liberalisation policies to attract **foreign investment** and improve their competitiveness in the global market.
 
• Examples of liberalisation include the **privatisation of state-owned enterprises** and deregulation of industries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Privatisation:**

 
 
• It involves the transfer of ownership of property or businesses from a government to a privately owned entity.
 
• Privatisation is often used to increase efficiency and productivity in the economy.
 
• Examples include the sale of government stakes in companies to private investors.
 
 
 
• **Deregulation:**
 
 
• It refers to the removal or simplification of government rules and regulations that constrain the operation of market forces.
 
• The goal is to increase the efficiency of markets and reduce the costs of compliance for businesses.
 
• Deregulation can be seen in sectors like airlines, telecommunications, and financial services.
 
 
 
• **Globalisation:**
 
 
• It is the process by which businesses or other organizations develop international influence or start operating on an international scale.
 
• Globalisation is often facilitated by liberalisation policies that open up economies to foreign trade and investment.
 
• It can lead to greater economic integration and interdependence among countries.
 
 
 
• **Economic Reforms of 1991:**
 
 
• India introduced significant economic reforms in 1991, which marked the beginning of liberalisation in the country.
 
• Key reforms included reducing trade tariffs, deregulating industries, and encouraging foreign direct investment (FDI).
 
• These reforms were aimed at making the Indian economy more market-oriented and expanding the role of private and foreign investment.
